analysis.title: weekly mash - Mark Wilson, 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: Thursday's post-midterm sell-off was a 4-4.9 sigma equity move. VIX had its 2nd largest 1-day move ever of vol of VIX, the largest number of US index puts ever traded, and the S&P had a 4 std dev move.

GS's Dems/Reps policy pair had been reflecting persistently higher implied risk since early summer. Wilson says the market is used to Trump-instigated policy volatility, but this episode requires pricing Democratic policy impetus, which may need a different reaction function.

Market structure amplified the move: over half of stocks are passively owned, much daily volume is price-agnostic quant, systematic, index and ETF trading, and fast-moving fundamental managers run leveraged strategies on similar risk models, so moves occur that standard sigma distributions would call improbable.

Correlations have been tested: Apple is negatively correlated with the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 has only a 60% correlation to the equal-weight S&P 500. NVDA realised 100 vol over the last 5 days and semis had a historic 5-day drawdown.
GS estimates Fundamental TMT funds were down 4% on Thursday and Multi-Strats down 140bps.

The stress was equity-specific. Per GS credit strategists, the generic 30y credit spread widened only 2.2bps while SPX fell 4.4% (8.2bp expected from regression), so credit's downside convexity has not kicked in yet.
GS credit strategists suggest shorting the generic IG 30Y basket on swap (rates hedged) against a beta-weighted long SPX future, to exploit the lower credit-equity beta while retaining liquidity.

The post-midterm sell-off hit AI spending beneficiaries, while hyperscalers rose. Per GS Asset & Wealth Management, 72 S&P 500 AI-infrastructure companies fell 13.3% in two days versus +1.7% for 5 hyperscalers, with the rest of the S&P flat. Credit supply concerns eased as datacentre build faces political friction.

AI spending beneficiaries' forward P/E fell to 13.1x, a 26% discount to the S&P 500's 17.8x. Both relative and absolute levels are the lowest since late 2022, even though their next-12-month earnings estimates have risen more than 50% relative to the S&P 500.
Rotation was severe: the hi-beta momentum factor had a >30% 4-week drawdown, is down 15% YTD and is 50%+ off its Q2 high. Monthly return dispersion between SPX-ex-AI and the SPX has widened.

10yr UST yields had become an AI-trade. Wilson expects AI to take a less prominent role as stocks have already been sold down, and expects realised volatility to fall as exposures are reduced. GS principal components work shows a meaningful growth de-rating and policy tightening already priced.
The market has rotated to safety: European defensives had their best month versus EuroStoxx on record. Pressure on consumer and rate-sensitive areas of the market has yet to reverse.

Wilson still favors the 1997/1998 analogy over 1999/2000. His supports: payrolls were robust, positioning has been hit hard, rates and oil are easing, and newly elected Democrats are unlikely to threaten aggregate growth.
His 25 Sept note argued that if stagflation is expected but goldilocks is delivered, equities should follow the historical pattern of gains from midterms to year-end.

Mega-cap tech rose versus broad AI and versus NDX, and regained half the ground lost versus the S&P in the prior 3 weeks. The market read policy as crimping capex, with supply discipline boosting pricing for constrained compute and datacentre capacity.

GS's US economist expects datacentre moratoria will not be long-lived if enacted, since data centres are low on voters' priority list. GS believes its US datacentre forecasts to 2029 are appropriately conservative.

Hyperscalers issued $67b of bonds across 5 deals in the last week, taking YTD issuance to $296b, almost $50b above GS's assumption for this year. GS has not cut its 2027 estimates. Wilson concludes the biggest issuers are likely ahead of themselves in funding and that financing supply ahead will come in below current estimates.

GS forecasts 2027 corporate EPS growth of 18%. Wilson notes lower rates, lower energy costs and a robust economy and labour market, and says not to write off 2026 continuing the 19/19 run of post-midterm equity rallies.

tension_points.bull_case: Payrolls were robust, positioning has been seriously hit, rates and oil are easing, newly elected Democrats are unlikely to threaten aggregate growth, and GS forecasts 18% 2027 EPS growth. Wilson holds to the 1997/1998 analogy and the 19/19 post-midterm rally record.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic policy impetus may need a different market reaction function. Datacentre moratoria threaten AI spending, market structure is fragile, credit has not yet repriced, and pressure on consumer and rate-sensitive areas has not reversed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 1999/2000-style path instead of 1997/1998, which Wilson says he does not expect.
